instructions: Rub a little of the oil over the inside of an 8 inch round or square cake pan. If the pan is aluminum or nonstick, line the bottom with a circle of parchment too.

Pour about 3 cups of water into a large pot that the cake pan fits inside with a little room around it, and set a rack or a trivet in the bottom. Cover it and bring the water to a boil over high while you make the batter.
Meanwhile, grate 1 tbsp of the ginger. Seed and mince 1 of the green chilies. Squeeze the lemon into a small cup. You need 2 tbsp of juice.

In a large bowl, whisk together 1 1/4 cups water, the 2 tbsp lemon juice, 3 tbsp of the sugar, 1 tsp of the salt, 2 tbsp of the oil, the grated ginger, the minced chili and the 2 tbsp semolina. Keep whisking until the sugar dissolves.

Set a sieve over the bowl and sift in the 2 cups besan and the 1/4 tsp turmeric. Whisk until the batter is smooth with no lumps, then keep whisking in one direction for about a minute more. Cover the bowl and leave the batter for 10 minutes.

Check that the water in the pot is boiling. Add the 1 1/2 tsp Eno and 1 tbsp water to the batter and stir quickly until it's mixed in. The batter will foam up and turn pale and thick. Stop stirring as soon as it's even.

Pour the batter straight into the greased pan and set the pan on the rack. Cover the pot, turn the heat to medium and steam for 18 to 20 minutes. No peeking for the first 15. It's done when a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Lift the pan out onto a wire rack and leave the dhokla to cool for about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, slit the other 2 green chilies down one side. Heat the last 1 tbsp oil in a small pan over medium and add the 1 tsp mustard seeds.
When the seeds start to pop, add the 12 curry leaves and the slit chilies. Stand back a little. They'll spatter.
Once the leaves turn crisp, after about 30 seconds, stir in the 1 tsp sesame seeds and cook for 1 minute. Add the 1/4 tsp asafoetida, the last 1 tbsp sugar, the last 1/2 tsp salt and 1 cup water.
Bring it to a boil and stir until the sugar dissolves, then turn off the heat. Leave it until it's just warm.
Run a knife around the edge of the cake pan, turn the dhokla out onto a tray and peel off the parchment if you used it. Cut it into 16 squares.
Spoon the chilies, curry leaves and seeds over the squares, then pour the tempering water slowly all over them. The squares will soak it up.
Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro and scatter it over the dhokla with the 2 tbsp coconut.
method_notes: All three read versions make an instant khaman: a besan and semolina batter soured with citric acid or lemon, raised with Eno right before it goes into a greased pan, steamed until a toothpick comes out clean, then soaked in a sweet tempering of mustard seeds, curry leaves and green chili in water. Swasthi's Recipes (the lead) uses 2 cups besan and 2 tbsp semolina, rests the batter 10 minutes, steams an 8 inch pan for 18 minutes and pours about a cup of tempering water over it once it's cool. Cook with Manali uses less besan, adds baking soda alongside the Eno and a much smaller splash of tempering water, and Cook with Kushi uses lemon juice, steams for 20 minutes and pours the tempering in two goes. This one follows the lead with lemon juice in place of citric acid, which the lead lists as an option, and only one chili in the batter.
